articles.title: Rochdale AFC Invites Community Feedback on Bowlee Hub Proposal
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC is seeking input from local residents and stakeholders on plans for a new Community Football & Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee, with the planning application currently under review by Rochdale Borough Council.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC is inviting supporters, local residents, community groups, and stakeholders to provide feedback on proposals for a new Community Football & Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee. The planning application is currently under consideration by Rochdale Borough Council.

The proposed hub aims to enhance community engagement and promote health and wellbeing through football and related activities. This initiative reflects the club's commitment to supporting local development.

Residents and stakeholders can participate in the consultation process by submitting their opinions and suggestions through the club's official channels. This is an opportunity for the community to influence the development of a facility that could benefit many.

The deadline for submissions has not been specified, but interested parties are encouraged to act promptly to ensure their voices are heard. Further details can be found on the Rochdale AFC website.

articles.excerpt: Rochdale-based Zen Internet has launched new 2.5Gbps broadband packages and Wi-Fi 7 routers, enhancing connectivity options for local residents and businesses.

Zen Internet, a Rochdale-based internet service provider, has launched new 2.5Gbps broadband packages and Wi-Fi 7 routers. This expansion aims to improve internet connectivity for customers in the UK, particularly in areas serviced by MS3's full fibre network.

The new broadband service is currently available in parts of Hull and Lincolnshire, following Zen's partnership with MS3, which began in June 2026. The introduction of Wi-Fi 7 routers is expected to provide faster and more reliable wireless connections.

Local residents and businesses in Rochdale may benefit from these advancements, as the increased speeds could support more devices and enhance overall internet performance.

Zen Internet is committed to expanding its services further in the coming months. Customers interested in upgrading their internet service can find more information on Zen Internet's website.

articles.title: Rochdale Procurement 360 Summit to Support Local Businesses in Securing Public Contracts
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Procurement 360 Summit, organised by Rochdale Development Agency, will take place on October 7 at Crown Oil Arena, aiming to help local businesses secure public-sector contracts.
articles.content_html:
An event aimed at assisting businesses in Rochdale to secure public-sector contracts is scheduled for Wednesday, October 7. The Rochdale Procurement 360 Summit will be held at Rochdale AFC’s Crown Oil Arena, organised by the Rochdale Development Agency (RDA).

The summit will feature keynote presentations, expert panel discussions, and networking opportunities, providing attendees with insights into public sector procurement processes. Participants will learn what buyers seek in successful bids, how to create meaningful social value, and how to identify commissioning opportunities within the public sector.

RDA stated that billions of pounds are spent annually through public sector procurement, and the summit aims to connect local businesses with public-sector organisations and procurement professionals. This initiative is part of Rochdale's strategy to enhance the value of contracts secured by local businesses, thereby fostering job creation and improving productivity within the borough.

STAR Procurement will also participate in the event, offering practical insights and answering questions related to procurement and bidding. This summit is designed for both established suppliers and those looking to enter the public sector market, ensuring that local businesses are well-equipped to compete for future contracts.

articles.title: New Endangered Wildlife Mural Unveiled in Middleton
articles.excerpt: A striking 15-metre-high wildlife mural has been unveiled on Oldham Road in Middleton, created through an international arts exchange project involving artists from Rochdale and Kenya.
articles.content_html:
A new wildlife mural measuring 15 metres high has been unveiled on Oldham Road in Middleton town centre. The artwork is part of the Endangered Exchange project, which focuses on raising awareness about endangered species and ecosystems. It was created by Rochdale artist Hayley Garner, known as AYLO, alongside Victoria Firth, founder of The Wild Mural Project, local artist Jamie Buckley, and Kenyan artist Ninah Tanya.

The mural features various endangered species, including a hen harrier, large heath butterfly, emperor dragonfly, and sphagnum moss, along with the phrase "Save our tomorrow today" presented in both English and Swahili. The design incorporates Kanga fabric, which is significant to Kenyan culture. Garner explained that the project aims to foster a deeper connection between communities and the planet through vibrant, community-driven art.

Ninah Tanya, who travelled from Nairobi for a two-week artist residency, expressed her excitement about working on the mural, stating it was the largest she had ever completed. She has been mentored by Firth over the past year and has also visited Rochdale to see other murals created by admired artists. Jamie Buckley is set to travel to Kenya next month to continue the exchange, where he will collaborate on workshops and a second mural focused on Kenya's natural environment.

Councillor Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, highlighted the mural as a powerful reminder of the challenges posed by climate change. The project is part of the Rochdale Creates cultural programme and is supported by various local organisations, including The Butterfly Effected CIC and Rochdale Development Agency. A documentary is being produced to capture the artists' journeys and the cultural exchange.

articles.title: M62 Traffic Delays Near Rochdale Due to Breakdown
articles.excerpt: Drivers faced significant delays on the M62 eastbound near Rochdale today, with queues stretching five miles following a breakdown. The incident has since cleared, but congestion remains.
articles.content_html:
Drivers experienced long delays on the M62 eastbound near Rochdale this afternoon, September 14, due to a breakdown that closed one lane of traffic. The incident occurred between junctions 20 and 21, leading to queues extending five miles and delays of approximately 35 minutes, according to National Highways.

Traffic Officers and recovery services were dispatched to the scene to manage the situation. A post on the National Highways North West Twitter account confirmed the lane closure and the ongoing congestion, advising drivers to expect delays as they approached the affected area.

As of the latest updates, the breakdown has been resolved, but residual delays remain, with traffic tailing back past junction 19 at Heywood. Motorists are advised to remain cautious and expect slower travel times as the traffic gradually clears.

This incident highlights the potential for traffic disruptions on major routes like the M62, particularly during peak travel times. Drivers planning to use this route may want to consider alternative paths or allow extra time for their journeys.

articles.title: Littleborough and Wardle Brass Bands Prepare for National Finals on 20 September
articles.excerpt: Littleborough Brass Band and Wardle Community Band showcased their test pieces at a concert in Dearnley ahead of the National Brass Band Championships of Great Britain at York Barbican.
articles.content_html:
Littleborough Brass Band and Wardle Community Band are gearing up for the National Brass Band Championships of Great Britain, taking place on Sunday, 20 September, at York Barbican. Both bands performed their test pieces during a concert held at St Andrew’s Church in Dearnley, Littleborough, on Sunday, 13 September.

Littleborough Brass Band, under the direction of conductor Max Stannard, played 'Snow Island' by Thierry Deleruyelle, competing in the Third Section. Meanwhile, Wardle Community Band, led by conductor Jane Conway, performed 'Heroes of the North' by Peter Graham, preparing for the Fourth Section contest.

Matthew Ryan, a brass band adjudicator and conductor, attended the concert to provide feedback to both bands on their performances. Jonathan Coomer, secretary of Littleborough Brass Band, emphasised the importance of performing in front of an audience as part of their preparation for the finals.

The concert attracted a full audience at St Andrew’s Church, showcasing the talent and dedication of both bands as they make their final preparations for the national competition this week.

articles.title: Inquest reveals details of fatal crash into Heywood pub after police chase
articles.excerpt: An inquest has heard that Will Place, 23, died after crashing into the White Lion pub in Heywood following a police pursuit that reached speeds of 70mph.
articles.content_html:
An inquest at Rochdale Coroner's Court has revealed that Will Place, 23, died after crashing into the White Lion pub in Heywood during a police chase on 1 July 2024. The incident occurred shortly after Place had been celebrating England's Euro 2024 victory, having been drinking while watching the match against Slovakia.

The court heard that Place got behind the wheel of his car at approximately 03:00 BST the following day. Police in a marked van initiated a pursuit after observing him run a red light on Manchester Road. CCTV footage presented at the inquest showed Place driving at speeds of up to 70mph through residential areas before police decided to call off the chase.

Despite the pursuit being terminated, Place continued driving and ultimately lost control of his vehicle, crashing into the pub. Emergency services arrived approximately 70 seconds later, but the car had already caught fire, leading to a partial collapse of the building. Place was pronounced dead shortly after 04:00.

A post-mortem examination revealed that Place had suffered catastrophic injuries and was found to be twice the legal limit for alcohol consumption at the time of the crash.
